newsitem.title: USA: Clinton opposes indexing of capital gains - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Clinton opposes indexing of capital gains - WSJ.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said he would not sign a tax bill that contains indexing of capital gains for inflation, contending it would be too costly, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Thursday's electronic edition, Clinton told the Journal in an interview that he believes the Republican-backed measure would violate the budget agreement with Congress that seeks a balanced budget by 2002.
"I have never seen any revenue estimates that don't show that you get a massive explosion in revenue loss," Clinton said.
The president said he has several other concerns about the Republican tax bills, but would wait to allow the process to continue before raising strong objections.
The Senate Finance Committee was expected to take up a version of the bill later Thursday that does not include indexing.

Clinton also said he favours expanding the tax deduction for individuals who work out of their homes, noting that the number of such people has grown to 12 million from the three million who existed when he was first elected in 1992.
Despite some of his objections with the Republican tax bills, Clinton said he believes that if Republicans stick to the negotiated budget deal, a bill can be crafted that he would sign.
"That's the only way we'll ever get there," he said. "If we abandon the agreement, then I don't know how we're going to get to a balanced budget. ..."
